item.case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
item.title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer

turns.text: Make a 60-second widescreen explainer video on the citric acid cycle (the Krebs cycle) for first-year biology students. Show the cycle as a loop inside a mitochondrion: acetyl-CoA enters and joins oxaloacetate to form citrate, two carbons leave as CO2, NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced along the way, and oxaloacetate is regenerated so the loop starts again. Label the key molecules on screen as they appear, under the title 'Citric acid cycle'. Calm English narration explaining each step as it happens. Simple clean 2D animation, no music.

stages.text:
Citric acid cycle
kind: explainer
style: 60-second widescreen explainer in simple, clean 2D animation using textbook-style diagrams; calm English narration; no music.
Under “Citric acid cycle,” an oval mitochondrial cutaway shows a symbolic, arrow-linked loop in the matrix. Labels identify molecules as calm English narration follows the reactions. Acetyl-CoA supplies a two-carbon acetyl group to four-carbon oxaloacetate, forming six-carbon citrate; CoA-SH is released.

Citrate rearranges into six-carbon isocitrate. Isocitrate becomes five-carbon α-ketoglutarate: CO₂ leaves and the first NADH appears. Next, four-carbon succinyl-CoA forms, releasing a second CO₂ and producing a second NADH. The departing carbons are not the newly arrived acetyl carbons.

Succinyl-CoA becomes succinate, releasing CoA-SH; a GTP → ATP callout represents one ATP equivalent, not two additional products. Membrane-embedded succinate dehydrogenase converts succinate to fumarate as FAD becomes FADH₂. Water enters as fumarate becomes malate.

Malate becomes oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH. The regenerated oxaloacetate can accept another acetyl group, closing the loop. The completed turn shows two CO₂, three NADH, one FADH₂ and one ATP equivalent.
stages.note: research: Citric acid cycle — research for one complete turn inside a mitochondrion, rather than a historical discovery episode. Follow acetyl-group entry, energy capture, carbon dioxide release and oxaloacetate regeneration. Dates below identify source publication dates, not dates when these recurring biochemical reactions occurred. The 60-second running time is a presentation choice, not the measured duration of one turn.

items.prompt:
Simple clean 2D animation, no music. One continuous 16:9 shot: an oval mitochondrial cutaway, double membrane, folded inner membrane and pale matrix containing a clockwise pathway diagram, not a physical ring. All labels are large navy type on white backing beside their objects; they persist to the end. A calm adult English narrator, called Narrator, speaks slowly and evenly; all quoted speech below is exact.
0–5 s: Title beat: hold "Citric acid cycle" at top center, stationary through 60 s. Reveal the cutaway beneath. Narrator: "The citric acid cycle takes place inside the mitochondrion."
5–17 s: Label entering "Acetyl-CoA", the four-dot starting group "Oxaloacetate", and the joined six-dot group "Citrate". Only the two-dot acetyl group joins; its CoA tail detaches. Narrator: "Acetyl-CoA supplies two carbons, joining four-carbon oxaloacetate to form citrate."
17–30 s: Citrate rearranges. At two successive arrows, six dots become five, then four. Each releases one "CO2" badge and one "NADH" badge. Release original oxaloacetate dots, not the incoming pair. Narrator: "Citrate rearranges. Two reactions each release carbon dioxide and produce NADH."
30–38 s: At the next arrow, one badge appears: "GTP → ATP". Narrator: "Next, energy is captured as GTP, which can transfer it to ATP."
38–46 s: Highlight the next arrow; emit "FADH2". Narrator: "The next oxidation produces FADH2. Water is then added."
46–55 s: Four dots return to the starting position; emit a third NADH badge. Narrator: "Another NADH forms as oxaloacetate is regenerated."
55–60 s: Another acetyl group approaches; pulse the closed loop. Narrator: "Oxaloacetate accepts another acetyl group, restarting the cycle."
No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles.
